decision.summary: The Federal Reserve held its target interest rate at 3.0 percent while launching major coordinated international liquidity measures.

changes.quote: FOMC statement: Federal Reserve and other central banks announce specific measures designed to address liquidity pressures in funding markets
changes.explanation: The Federal Reserve and global central banks issued a special statement to address severe liquidity pressures in financial markets.

changes.quote: Since the coordinated actions taken in December 2007, the G-10 central banks have continued to work together closely and to consult regularly on liquidity pressures in funding markets.
changes.explanation: Major central banks have maintained close coordination since December 2007 to monitor ongoing stresses.

changes.quote: Pressures in some of these markets have recently increased again.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that financial market strains have worsened recently, prompting new interventions.

changes.quote: Under this new Term Securities Lending Facility (TSLF), the Federal Reserve will lend up to $200 billion of Treasury securities to primary dealers secured for a term of 28 days (rather than overnight, as in the existing program) by a pledge of other securities, including federal agency debt, federal agency residential-mortgage-backed securities (MBS), and non-agency AAA/Aaa-rated private-label residential MBS.
changes.explanation: The Fed created a $200 billion lending facility allowing dealers to swap riskier mortgage-backed securities for safer Treasury bonds for 28 days.

changes.quote: In addition, the Federal Open Market Committee has authorized increases in its existing temporary reciprocal currency arrangements (swap lines) with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Swiss National Bank (SNB).
changes.explanation: The Fed expanded emergency dollar swap lines with international central banks to ease global funding pressures.

tone_quotes.quote: Pressures in some of these markets have recently increased again.
We all continue to work together and will take appropriate steps to address those liquidity pressures.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.75% APR costs about $53.12 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.6% and moved +14 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.24% would rise by about $27.39 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.9%, and employers added an average of 13k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.1% over the past year (February 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +27 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: This emergency statement signals that the Committee is prioritizing financial stability and liquidity backstops over normal interest rate adjustments.
